speaker: Swami Sivananda
title: Association with holy company (Satsang)
text: Give up bad company, smoking, meat and alcoholic liquors entirely. Have constant Satsang (association with holy people). Do not develop any evil habits. Deliberately exert to develop positive virtuous qualities.
modern_interpretation: To foster profound personal growth and well-being, consciously disengage from all forms of detrimental associations and self-destructive habits, such as negative peer influence, smoking, unhealthy dietary choices, and excessive alcohol consumption. Instead, make a deliberate effort to surround yourself with positive, uplifting individuals (Satsang) and actively cultivate virtuous qualities that align with your highest potential.
summary: This instruction emphasizes the critical importance of entirely abandoning all negative habits and associations while actively seeking out positive company and consciously developing virtuous qualities for holistic self-improvement and spiritual advancement.
actionable_advice: Identify one significant detrimental habit or negative association in your life and commit to its complete cessation, while simultaneously joining a supportive community or mentorship program that encourages positive character development and virtuous living.
embedding_ready_text: Swami Sivananda's instruction, 'Give up bad company, smoking, meat and alcoholic liquors entirely. Have constant Satsang (association with holy people). Do not develop any evil habits. Deliberately exert to develop positive virtuous qualities,' is a powerful call to transform oneself. This timeless wisdom, translated for modern understanding, encourages individuals, especially youth, to consciously disengage from all self-destructive habits and negative influences, such as unhealthy lifestyle choices or toxic peer pressure. Simultaneously, it advocates for actively seeking out positive, uplifting communities and intentionally cultivating beneficial character traits through consistent effort. This guidance directly addresses feelings of `lack_of_direction`, `low_self_esteem`, `impulsivity`, and `addiction`, offering clear `discipline` and `mind_control` strategies to foster `self_worth`, `purpose`, and `clarity` through `transformative` self-growth and `ethical` living, aligning with `yogic` and `stoic` principles of virtue and `inner_purity`.
